environmental-score.description: How good each street is for cycling (0–100): smooth surface, safe overtaking, clean air, few stops, etc. Higher is better.

overview.title: Explore your city's environment
overview.subtitle: See what matters for cycling: air, road surface, traffic, shade and lighting. Turn layers on and off and click an area for details.
overview.streetLayersHint: Layers that colour the streets are shown one at a time.
overview.detailsEmpty: Click an area on the map to see its measured indicators, data source and unit.
overview.areaNote: Area = 500 m × 500 m grid cell. Values are averages of the measurements inside it.
overview.indexNote: Risk indices are calculated by ATRAI from senseBox:bike sensor rides (0 = low, 1 = high). They are not concentrations in µg/m³.

planTrip.title: Find your greenest route
planTrip.subtitle: Compare the shortest route with a route planned around what you care about: smooth streets, safe overtaking, clean air and fewer stops.
planTrip.clickHint: Search for a place, or click the map: first the start, then the destination.
planTrip.preferTimeHint: Plans by riding time, using the speeds cyclists were measured at.
planTrip.departTimeHint: Needed for the shade and lighting sliders: shade counts by day, lighting after dark.
planTrip.comparisonPaused: Showing the trip with a rented vehicle on the map. This comparison is for riding your own bike, so it is greyed out until you switch the rental trip off.

routes.shortestHint: The most direct path, ignoring comfort.

metrics.scales: Roughness 0–100 · fine dust 0.5 = usual, higher = more dust · stop-and-go, shade and lit 0–1 (share of the way) · kcal a rough estimate.

tips.roughness: Estimated from nearby measured streets where sensor bikes didn’t ride.
tips.kcalNoHeight: no height data, climbs not counted
tips.kcal: For a 70 kg rider on a normal bike.

day.info: Shade is worked out for 09:00, 12:00, 15:00 and 18:00, and lit streets count after dark. So your route can only change at these times of day: pick one to see it.
day.label: Time of day
day.needRoute: Set a start and destination first.

planTrip.appliedShade: Departure by day: shaded streets were preferred.
planTrip.appliedDark: Departure after dark: lit streets were preferred.
planTrip.emptyState: Set a start and destination to compare routes. Values only appear when they come from real data.

legend.hint: One colour per band. Uphill turns yellow to orange already at 2–4 %, which you feel; red from 6 %, dark red at 10 % and more. Downhill is blue to violet: the darker, the more braking. Flat (under 1 %) is green.

compare.title: With and without your settings
compare.hint: Grey dashed on the map: the same trip with every slider at 0. The values for bumps, overtaking, air and stops are for the ride only. Each trip picks the quickest vehicle near your start, so the two can differ; an e-scooter only counts kcal where you push it.
compare.same: With your settings the trip is the same as without them.

info.dangerRow: up to {{m}} m detour per spot

bump.question: How much longer does a very bumpy street feel to you?
bump.note: Very bumpy = the bumpiest 10 % of streets measured in Heilbronn (roughness 20 or more). Bumpier ones count even more; typical or smoother ones nothing extra.
bump.example: With {{p}}, you’d ride up to {{m}} m extra to skip 100 m of very bumpy street.

danger.question: How far would you ride out of your way to pass one fewer close-overtaking spot?
danger.note: Spots where sensor bikes measured cars overtaking too closely. Riskier spots count more.

pm.question: How much longer does a street with bad air feel to you?
pm.note: Bad air = the worst 10 % of streets measured by the sensor bikes. Typical or cleaner air counts nothing extra.
pm.example: With {{p}}, you’d ride up to {{m}} m extra to skip 100 m of street with bad air.

stop.question: How much longer does a street with lots of stop-and-go feel to you?
stop.note: Lots of stop-and-go = the worst 10 % of streets (traffic lights, congestion). Each lift on the way also counts as {{lift}} m.
stop.example: With {{p}}, you’d ride up to {{m}} m extra to skip 100 m of heavy stop-and-go.

bikeFriendly.question: How much longer does a street without a bike path or lane feel to you?
bikeFriendly.note: Bike paths, bike lanes and signposted bike routes from OpenStreetMap.
bikeFriendly.example: With {{p}}, you’d ride up to {{m}} m extra to swap 100 m of ordinary street for a bike path or lane.

shade.question: By day: how much longer does a street in full sun feel to you?
shade.note: Half-shaded streets count half. Only used when the sun is up at your departure time. Shade is calculated for 21 July (09, 12, 15 and 18 h; the closest hour is used).
shade.example: With {{p}}, you’d ride up to {{m}} m extra to skip 100 m in full sun.

dark.question: After dark: how much longer does an unlit street feel to you?
dark.note: Streets that are probably lit count less. Only used with a departure time after sunset.
dark.example: With {{p}}, you’d ride up to {{m}} m extra to skip 100 m of unlit street.

sky.day: The sun is up then: shade counts, the lighting slider is off.
sky.night: It is dark then: lit streets count, the shade slider is off.
sky.summerShade: Shade is calculated for a summer day (21 July), so outside summer it shows which streets buildings and trees shade, not that day’s exact shadows.

why.title: Why this route?
why.same: It is also the shortest route: for your settings no detour is worth it ({{km}} km, {{min}} min). On the way:
why.trade: It is {{m}} m ({{pct}}) longer and {{time}} than the shortest route. In return:
why.bars: Grey: shortest route, {{shortest}}. Green: your route, {{yours}}.
why.mapHint: Point at a row to see where those streets are on the map; click it to keep them shown. Point at either route line to see what a street is like.

reports.title: Riders' reports
reports.info: One report makes routes avoid a street where there is a sensible way round; three riders close it for routing. A report counts through the date you give, else for a day. Two riders saying it is open again lift it. Footways and map mistakes wait for a maintainer to check them.

upload.title: Share your own route
upload.intro: Upload a ride you recorded with another app (a GPX file) and share it with everyone.
upload.howTo: How to get the GPX file

apps.komoot: Komoot: open your recorded tour → "…" → "Download" → GPX.
apps.strava: Strava (in the browser): open the activity → "…" → "Export GPX".
apps.garmin: Garmin Connect: open the activity → gear icon → "Export to GPX".

upload.rules: Recorded rides with timestamps only, no planned routes. The ride must pass through Heilbronn, be 1 to 200 km long and look like a bike ride. The first and last 200 m are not published, so nobody sees where you live.
upload.trimmed: The dashed line on the map is what everyone will see: without the first and last 200 m.
upload.name: Name
upload.descriptionPlaceholder: What makes the ride nice? Where is a good place for a break?
upload.publicNote: Once published, everyone sees the route with your display name. You can delete it on your profile at any time.

errors.invalid: This isn't a GPX file. Export the ride from your app as GPX.
errors.no_times: The file has no timestamps. Upload a recorded ride, not a planned route.
errors.too_short: The ride is shorter than 1 km.
errors.too_long: The ride is longer than 200 km.
errors.too_fast: The ride averages more than 40 km/h and doesn't look like a bike ride.
errors.outside: The ride must pass through Heilbronn and stay in the area around it.
errors.too_big: The file is larger than 5 MB.
